title: A trigonometric function and a graph: composites, every solution, and an inverse

stimulus.title: The graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = 2\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{4}\right) + 1</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Find the value of f(g(2))f(g(2)). Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: Inner value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2) = 3</annotation></semantics></math> shown, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(2)) = f(3) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2) = 2\sin\frac{\pi}{2} + 1 = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(3) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>
the inner value 3 written before the final value 3

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2(1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3</annotation></semantics></math>. From the graph, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(3) = 5 - 2(3 - 2) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(2)) = f(3) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find every value of xx in [0,8][0, 8] for which f(x)=1f(x) = 1.

rubric.point: All three values, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 7</annotation></semantics></math>, and no others

parts.sample: The horizontal line <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 1</annotation></semantics></math> meets the graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> three times: at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> on the first segment, at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math> on the second (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 - 2(x - 2) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>) and at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 7</annotation></semantics></math> on the third (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - 6 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>). So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 7</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Find every value of xx in [0,8][0, 8] for which g(x)=2.5g(x) = 2.5. Give each answer correct to three decimal places, and show the setup.

rubric.point: Sets up <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = 2.5</annotation></semantics></math> (or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{4}\right) = 0.75</annotation></semantics></math>) and gives one correct solution

Gives both solutions, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 1.080</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.920</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 2.920</annotation></semantics></math>, and no others in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{4}\right) + 1 = 2.5</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{4}\right) = 0.75</annotation></semantics></math>. In radian mode, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi x}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.75</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sin^{-1}(0.75)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>0.848062</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.848062</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>0.848062</mn><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.293531</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi - 0.848062 \approx 2.293531</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 1.080</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.920</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 2.920</annotation></semantics></math>. On <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[4, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{4}\right) \le 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so there are no other solutions (graphing <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = g(x)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2.5</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 8]</annotation></semantics></math> shows exactly two intersections).

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Is gg invertible on the interval [0,4][0, 4]? Give a reason for your answer using values of gg.

rubric.point: No, with two specific inputs in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 4]</annotation></semantics></math> that give the same output

parts.sample: No. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\sin\frac{\pi}{4} + 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sqrt{2} + 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\sin\frac{3\pi}{4} + 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sqrt{2} + 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Two different inputs in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 4]</annotation></semantics></math> share the output <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2} + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> has no inverse on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 4]</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: On the interval [−2,2][-2, 2], gg is invertible. Write an expression for g−1(x)g^{-1}(x), for −1≤x≤3-1 \le x \le 3.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{-1}(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{4}{\pi}\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x - 1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Swap and solve: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2\sin\left(\frac{\pi y}{4}\right) + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(\frac{\pi y}{4}\right) = \frac{x - 1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-2, 2]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi y}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>, the range of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi y}{4} = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x - 1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{-1}(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{4}{\pi}\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x - 1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
